answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a bond in a shared vault before it can trade. The bond is released only after a history of attested, settled work, so a new fake account starts as a dry oasis with no credit and cannot reach zenith reputation overnight. An attacker must fund and age thousands of bonds, pay slashing losses when duplicates are detected, and wait through the same slow earning curve as honest agents, making mass fakery cost more than any fraud it could enable.
